鋅是微量礦物質，與300種以上的酶有關。鋅是促進毛囊生長所需，低鋅可能脫髮。
膠原蛋白和角蛋白，也需要鋅。缺鋅，可能頭髮稀疏又脆弱。

成年人每天最多可攝入的鋅約40毫克，而不會有副作用。

要知道你是哪一種肥肚子、怎麼做，可減去腹部脂肪？ 0:00 簡介：腹部脂肪 0:30 了解腹部脂肪 1:38 第一類型肥肚子：下垂的肥肚子 5:05 第二類型肥肚子：凸出的肥肚子 7:50 第三類型肥肚子：鬆垮的肥肚子
柏格醫生dr berg 說明：三類型的肥肚子 1. 下垂的肚子 這是內臟脂肪從肝臟、從器官周圍、內部溢出。這是一種危險的脂肪類型，因會阻礙某些器官的功能，讓發炎加劇，產生其他的健康問題。
這類型的肚子通常是吃太多的碳水或過多的壓力（皮質醇）觸發了胰島素引起的。想要擺脫這種肚子，吃低碳水和紓解壓力。
2. 凸出的肚子 這實際上並不胖。凸出的肚子可能是肝臟長期有問題引起的。肝臟受傷，體液從肝臟流到腹腔囊袋，必須立即改變生活方式。
生育三烯酚(tocotrienols)形式的維生素E，對肝硬化有幫助。 每天服用2-3次，每次300毫克。 食用十字花科蔬菜和適量的蛋白質也很好。 體內的菌群也很重要。 吃牛磺熊去氧膽酸（TUDCA）， 注重飲食，避免某些食物。
3. 鬆垮的肚子 這是表皮脂肪。通常是因為過多雌激素(estrogen)引起的。這種類型的脂肪很常見，並不危險。

柏格醫生 dr berg 說明糖尿病、減肥和燃燒脂肪，缺一種最重要的營養素。
糖尿病有高血糖、胰島素阻抗和高低起伏的胰島素。
高血糖的症狀： 1. 口渴增加 2. 排尿增多（尤其是在夜晚） 3. 疲勞（尤其是進食後） 4. 模糊的視野 5. 飢餓 6. 渴望（尤其是碳水化合物） 7. 情緒變化（憤怒或悲傷）
胰島素需要鉀來幫助調節或降低血糖。如果有胰島素阻抗，需要更多的鉀來平衡你的血糖。
缺鉀會使血糖越來越高。葡萄糖也需要鉀才能進入細胞。如葡萄糖不能進入細胞，就會開始積聚，導致高血糖。
缺鉀還會使您患糖尿病、胰島素阻抗、體重增加、高膽固醇、高三酸甘油酯和脂肪肝的風險更高。身體每天需要 4,700 毫克鉀。
缺鉀的原因： 1. 精製碳水化合物和糖 2. 味精 3. 利尿劑 4. 壓力 5. 糖尿病 6. 運動
鉀是最重要的礦物質，有助於調節血糖並減少對藥物的需求。
高鉀食物： 1. 皇帝豆（Lima beans,不適合生酮飲食） 2. 酪梨 3. 哈密瓜（不適合生酮飲食） 4. 黑糖（不適合生酮） 5. 甜菜根（草酸鹽含量高） 6. 綠葉蔬菜
食用綠葉蔬菜是獲取鉀的最佳方式。 優質的電解質粉，也是補鉀的好方法。

柏格醫生 Dr Berg 談：如何延緩衰老，讓您看起來更年輕、更長壽。 粒線體是人體的能量工廠。 粒線體的健康和功能與老化和壽命直接相關。
克氏循環 (Krebs cycle) 是身體內的一個過程，以食物開始，以能量結束。 它需要營養素或輔助因子才能正常運作。 NAD 是一種重要的營養素，參與從食物中提取能量以製造 ATP (細胞能量)，對於長壽和抗衰老，至關重要。
NAD 可防止肌肉損失，尤其是癌症患者的肌肉損失，並可防止輻射。 隨著年齡的增長，NAD 會減少。 研究人員發現，CD38 會消耗 NAD，而 CD38 較少的小白鼠壽命較長。
以下是 5 種可增強 NAD 並有助於延緩老化的化合物：
1.芹菜素 (Apigenin) 香菜是最好的來源，但百里香、牛至 (Oregano)、羅勒和西洋芹也有。
2.花黃素 (Anthoxanthin) 藍莓和其他藍色、紫色或紅色食物，如接骨木莓 (Elderberry)、康科德 (Concord) 葡萄和紫薯。
3.薑黃素 (Curcumin) 存在薑黃中
4.槲皮素 (Quercetin) 最好的來源是洋蔥，大部分槲皮素在洋蔥外層。 蘋果皮也有槲皮素。
5.亞甲藍 (Methylene blue) 是有史以來發明的第一種藥物。 似乎是一種很好的 CD38 抑制劑，可以幫助增強 NAD。

亞甲藍(Methylene blue)不是天然的，但有一些神奇的特性。了解亞甲藍的潛在健康好處。
柏格醫生 dr berg 談：亞甲藍 (Methylene blue)。 之前沒有談過，因為它不是自然療法——它實際上是一種合成藥物。但，它有一些有趣的特性。
亞甲藍在一般藥局販售，已經很長一段時間了。 它是醫學上第一種完全合成的藥物，最早的抗生素之一、也是最早的抗精神病藥物之一。
亞甲藍也被用於治療瘧疾，目前用於治療氰化物中毒和一氧化碳中毒。在低劑量下，亞甲藍可當作抗氧化劑。
亞甲藍有助於某些症狀，包括： 1. 敗血性休克 2. 過敏反應 3. 病毒 4. 疲勞 5. 腦霧 6. 記憶力減退 7. 憂鬱 8. 念珠菌 9. 神經退化 10. 痛風 11. 修復線粒體 (Mitochondrial)受損 12. 消炎 如你決定嘗試亞甲藍，我建議使用 USP(美國藥典)等級 1%的溶液。每滴約 0.5 毫克。
吃 SSRI(抗憂鬱藥)的人，不要吃亞甲藍。 試用此療法前，請先諮詢你的醫生，確保沒有禁忌症。

ns2:group.ns2:title: [Keynote] Different clocks Why execution speed is a strategic choice
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Over the past 18 months, MYOB built an AI product capability from the ground up: New teams, new platforms, new operating rhythms, and a growing portfolio of customer-facing AI products. The most important decisions weren’t technical. They were strategic.
This talk explores how MYOB matched the pace of decisions to the pace of change: When to hack around legacy systems, standardize or stay flexible, build or buy, reshape teams, and prioritize learning over shipping. The goal isn’t simply to move faster, but to know what deserves to move fast — and what deserves time to compound.
AI moves fast, but not every decision should.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Agents don't fail, they guess: Designing contracts for multi-agent pipelines – Amit Upadhyay

ns2:group.ns2:title: Agents don't fail, they guess: Designing contracts for multi-agent pipelines – Amit Upadhyay
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Multi-agent pipelines fail differently from single agents. One agent gets it wrong and you see it. A pipeline compounds wrong assumptions invisibly — each agent confidently consuming the uncertain output of the last.
This is the contract problem: when one agent's output is another's input, how do you encode what it doesn't know?
We built and deployed this in production. Two agents, one analysing, one transforming, passing a typed contract between them. Every field carries a confidence level. A gating mechanism stops the pipeline when certainty falls below threshold.
Agents don't fail — they guess. Build your contracts like that's true.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/xconf

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]AI is a scout, not an engineer – Tyson Brown

ns2:group.ns2:title: AI is a scout, not an engineer – Tyson Brown
ns2:group.ns2:description:
I spent 26 months building a distributed database in Rust with heavy AI help. Three times, AI nearly broke it. Code that compiled, passed tests, benchmarked well, but would have corrupted data in production. Each failure looked like success.
The consensus says AI takes the coding while humans move up to design and testing. It's backwards. AI belongs on the disposable edges. Humans belong in the middle, holding the understanding no test can verify from outside.
This talk is those three near-misses, the research behind them, and Human Replay: the method that keeps the understanding yours.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/xconf

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Beyond GPUs: Building the engineering platform for the AI factory – Shangqi Liu

ns2:group.ns2:title: Beyond GPUs: Building the engineering platform for the AI factory – Shangqi Liu
ns2:group.ns2:description:
AI factories promise massive compute, but GPUs alone do not create a productive AI platform. The challenge is to make thousands of accelerators, networks, power systems, cooling infrastructure, and facilities operate as one reliable, efficient system.
Drawing on first-hand experience building AI datacenter infrastructure, this talk explores the engineering platform behind the AI factory: Kubernetes, topology-aware orchestration, inference serving, developer workflows, high-resolution telemetry, resilient data pipelines, and power/grid-aware scheduling. We examine the architectural principles and trade-offs required to turn scarce, expensive infrastructure into production AI that is operable, scalable, and trustworthy.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]First Responder: Agentic incident triage – Vijay More

ns2:group.ns2:title: First Responder: Agentic incident triage – Vijay More
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Production incidents are costly, chaotic, and deeply manual. Engineers sift through logs, metrics, configs, and code under pressure, often with no clear starting point. Agentic AI changes that.
In this talk, Vijay presents a live demo of First Responder, an agentic system that investigates production incidents end-to-end. Starting from an alert, automatic triaging and closes the loop with automated fix generation and pull request creation, with engineers staying in control throughout.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]From dead-on-arrival to alive: How AI resurrects the humble ADR – Xiaowen Zhuang and Hao Pan

ns2:group.ns2:title: From dead-on-arrival to alive: How AI resurrects the humble ADR – Xiaowen Zhuang and Hao Pan
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Architecture Decision Records often die the moment they are written: approved, archived, and quickly ignored as teams and systems evolve. In the age of AI, that could change.
In this talk, two solution architects show how ADRs can become living, versioned specifications that guide implementation, shape AI-assisted workflows, and support continuous governance across many teams. We explore how documents become machine-consumable context, how architectural intent can be traced into code and review loops, and how AI can help reduce drift. The deeper shift is socio-technical: designing not just systems, but the environment that keeps them aligned.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Keeping sight of the customer in AI-first delivery – Kate Linton

ns2:group.ns2:title: Keeping sight of the customer in AI-first delivery – Kate Linton
ns2:group.ns2:description:
As AI agents rush into every product roadmap, it’s become dangerously easy to optimise for what AI can do, rather than what people actually need. Many teams are shipping AI-first features that are impressive in demos but fragile in the real world: eroding trust, amplifying bias, or quietly adding cognitive load.
In this talk, I’ll share a practical approach to keeping humans at the centre of AI-first product design. We’ll look at how to frame problems in human terms before choosing models, how to design for consent, control and transparency, and how to use guardrails and hypothesis-led experimentation to balance desirability with safety, accountability and economic impact.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/xconf

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Making chatbots sweat: Testing AI conversations at scale – Bishnu Prasad and Pratyush Mittal

ns2:group.ns2:title: Making chatbots sweat: Testing AI conversations at scale – Bishnu Prasad and Pratyush Mittal
ns2:group.ns2:description:
AI chatbots now handle our banking, healthcare, and support but how do we know they're safe? Unlike traditional software, the same question can get a helpful answer one moment and a wrong, unsafe, or manipulated one the next, and a human tester chatting for an hour barely scratches the surface.
This talk introduces AI SimTest: an engine that uses AI to test AI. It generates hundreds of simulated users, including adversarial ones, runs real conversations against any bot, and judges every response for accuracy, safety, and compliance. We'll show how "AI testing AI" catches failures before real people do.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/xconf

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]The AI native squad: How small teams deliver faster with AI – Jessie Xia and Siyuan Li

ns2:group.ns2:title: The AI native squad: How small teams deliver faster with AI – Jessie Xia and Siyuan Li
ns2:group.ns2:description:
AI is changing software delivery, but the real breakthrough is not just making individual developers faster. It is redesigning delivery around AI-native squads.
In this talk, Jessie Xia and Siyuan Li will share how small, high-transparency teams of 3–6 people can deliver business outcomes faster by embedding AI across every role — product engineer, quality manager, and domain expertise. Through real delivery examples, they will show how team structure, ceremonies, and daily workflows change when AI becomes a shared team capability.
The talk will also look ahead to harness-driven agentic delivery, where humans guide intent and quality while autonomous agents assist with execution. Mastering the AI-native squad model today is the foundation for the future of software delivery.
http://www.thoughtworks.com/xconf

薑黃烹飪過後，營養會被破壞嗎？ 薑黃是發炎和許多症狀的天然療法。但有人說薑黃不能加熱，因會破壞植物營養素，這是錯誤的說法。 時間標示： 0:00 簡介：薑黃的傳說 0:18 加熱會破壞薑黃的植物營養素嗎？ 2:25 薑黃含三種超強的植物營養素。 3:28 分享你的成功心得！
你可能認為加熱會破壞所有的化合物。但是某些草藥，加熱可增強一些植物營養素。
一項有趣的研究，測試了在180攝氏度或356華氏度的溫度下烘烤、煮沸和烹飪薑黃70分鐘。並測量了總抗氧化力。

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [TED]Why We Should Design Cities Like Disney | Zach DeBoer | TED

ns2:group.ns2:title: Why We Should Design Cities Like Disney | Zach DeBoer | TED
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Where you live shapes your relationships, your emotions and even how long you live, says community designer Zach DeBoer. After studying what a century of building cities around cars has done to downtowns in the US, he turned to lessons from some of the most walkable, carefully designed streets in the country: the ones inside Disney theme parks. With ideas ranging from narrower roads to buildings that pull you around the next corner, he offers a practical guide to turning ordinary downtowns into magical places people want to explore. (Recorded at TEDxSioux Falls on May 5, 2023)
